title: Natural numbers as sets: infinity, induction, and arithmetic
summary: The least inductive set realizes the natural numbers and their unique arithmetic structure.
abstract: Zero can be represented by the empty set, one by the set containing zero, and two by the set containing zero and one. Continuing this pattern makes each natural number the set of all its predecessors. The axiom of infinity puts all these stages inside one set; the smallest set containing zero and closed under successor satisfies induction. Addition and multiplication then arise from recursive definitions.
